Based on the clues you shared, the castle you’re thinking of is most likely the **Alcazaba of Almería** (also frequently just called the *Alcazaba de Almería*). Here is why it fits the description: | Feature | How it matches the Alcazaba | |---------|-----------------------------| | **South‑Europe location, near the sea** | Almería is in the south‑east of Spain, while the Alcazaba sits on a rocky spur that overlooks the Mediterranean Sea. The sea is roughly 0.5–0.8 km from the castle’s western side. | | **Two “theatres” within walking distance (600‑1,100 m)** | The town of Almería has two major public‑theatre venues that are easily reached from the Alcazaba’s main entrance:
• **Teatro de Almería** – a historic wooden‑timber theatre built in 1884, about **600 m** north of the castle.
• **Almería Auditorium (Auditorio de Almería)** – a modern multi‑purpose concert hall, roughly **900 m** to the north‑west of the Alcazaba. Both are well within your stated 600‑1,100 m walking range.| | **A church a couple hundred metres to the northeast of the main entrance** | The **Catholic Cathedral of Almería** (Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepción) lies just a few hundred metres northeast of the Alcazaba’s main (white‑washed) gate. Its spire can be seen from the castle’s southern terrace. | | **The sea a few hundred metres further but < 1 km away** | Starting from the cathedral at the far end of the Alcazaba, the sandy beach of Almería (Cala de los Cármenes / Playa de los Campos) is only about 200–250 m to the southeast, and the Mediterranean itself is a total of less than 1 km from the main entrance of the Alcazaba. | **Why the Alcazaba is a great next destination** * **Historical layers** – From its Umayyad (Almohad) origins to its Roman foundations, the Alcazaba offers a vivid palimpsest of Iberian history. * **Panoramic views** – The ruined walls give stunning views of the city, the cathedral, and the distant sea. * **Nearby attractions** – Inside the town itself you’ll find the two mentioned theatres, the cathedral, the old city (“Casco Antiguo”), and picturesque street cafés. The beaches are a short walk or bus ride from the castle. If you’re looking to revisit the region, the Alcazaba of Almería is a distinctly Mediterranean castle that neatly matches every detail you recall. Happy planning!

Based on the clues you shared, the castle you’re thinking of is most likely the **Alcazaba of Almería** (also frequently just called the *Alcazaba de Almería*). Here is why it fits the description: | Feature | How it matches the Alcazaba | |---------|-----------------------------| | **South‑Europe location, near the sea** | Almería is in the south‑east of Spain, while the Alcazaba sits on a rocky spur that overlooks the Mediterranean Sea. The sea is roughly 0.5–0.8 km from the castle’s western side. | | **Two “theatres” within walking distance (600‑1,100 m)** | The town of Almería has two major public‑theatre venues that are easily reached from the Alcazaba’s main entrance:
• **Teatro de Almería** – a historic wooden‑timber theatre built in 1884, about **600 m** north of the castle.
• **Almería Auditorium (Auditorio de Almería)** – a modern multi‑purpose concert hall, roughly **900 m** to the north‑west of the Alcazaba. Both are well within your stated 600‑1,100 m walking range.| | **A church a couple hundred metres to the northeast of the main entrance** | The **Catholic Cathedral of Almería** (Catedral de la Inmaculada Concepción) lies just a few hundred metres northeast of the Alcazaba’s main (white‑washed) gate. Its spire can be seen from the castle’s southern terrace. | | **The sea a few hundred metres further but < 1 km away** | Starting from the cathedral at the far end of the Alcazaba, the sandy beach of Almería (Cala de los Cármenes / Playa de los Campos) is only about 200–250 m to the southeast, and the Mediterranean itself is a total of less than 1 km from the main entrance of the Alcazaba. | **Why the Alcazaba is a great next destination** * **Historical layers** – From its Umayyad (Almohad) origins to its Roman foundations, the Alcazaba offers a vivid palimpsest of Iberian history. * **Panoramic views** – The ruined walls give stunning views of the city, the cathedral, and the distant sea. * **Nearby attractions** – Inside the town itself you’ll find the two mentioned theatres, the cathedral, the old city (“Casco Antiguo”), and picturesque street cafés. The beaches are a short walk or bus ride from the castle. If you’re looking to revisit the region, the Alcazaba of Almería is a distinctly Mediterranean castle that neatly matches every detail you recall. Happy planning!
